sentences.text:
National Insurance Co Ltd vs Master Avinash & Ors on 23
March, 2023

Author: Rekha Palli
Bench: Rekha Palli
 $~10
 * In The High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi
 + Mac.App. 527/2018 & Cm Appl. 23314/2018 -Stay
 National Insurance Co Ltd .....

entities.text: High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Appellan
 Through: Mr.Pradeep Gaur with Ms.Sweta
 Sinha, Advs.
 versus
 Master Avinash & Ors .....

Respondent
 Through: Mr.Satya Narayan with Ms.Babita,
 Advs.
 Coram:
 Hon'Ble Ms. Justice Rekha Palli
 Order
The present appeal preferred by the Insurer under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act assails the award dated 29.01.2018 passed by the learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal.
Vide the impugned award, the learned Tribunal has dealt with three claim petitions in respect of three persons, who expired in the same fateful accident on 13.12.2016.

As the appellant/insurance company has preferred three separate appeals in respect of all the three claims, the present appeal is confined only to the compensation awarded on account of the death of Smt.Seema Devi a house-wife, who lost her life in the fateful accident.

2. Vide the impugned award, the learned Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.21,58,600/- along with interest @ 9% per annum as compensation to respondent nos. 1 to 5, under the head loss of dependency by taking her monthly income as Rs.8,890/-.
The relevant extract of the impugned award reads as under- - "42. Loss of dependency: In the present case, deceased was aged less than 40 years.
Hence, as per mandate of 'Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd Vs Manmeet Singh (supra), there should be an addition of 25% in the income of deceased.

entities.text: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd Vs Manmeet Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, loss of dependency comes out to (Rs.8,890/- plus 25% of Rs.8,890/-) X 12 X 16 = Rs.21,33,600/-.
As per directions in 'Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd Vs Manmeet Singh' (supra), only a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded towards loss of love and affection.

entities.text: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd Vs Manmeet Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, petitioners are National Insurance Co Ltd vs Master Avinash & Ors on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53856508/
1 awarded a total compensation of Rs.21,58,600/- (Rs. Twenty One Lac Fifty Eight Thousand and Six Hundred Only)."

entities.text: National Insurance Co Ltd vs Master Avinash & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. In support of the appeal, Mr.Gaur, learned counsel for the appellant has raised four grounds, his first contention being that no eye-witness to prove that the driver of the offending truck was driving rashly and negligently having been examined by the claimants, no finding of rash and negligent driving by the driver of insured vehicle could have been given.

He next submits and there being four pillion riders, along with the deceased on the motor-cycle at the time of the accident, it was evident that the deceased had himself violated traffic rules and therefore no compensation was payable by the appellant.

4. He next submits that Smt.Seema Devi being a house-wife, no notional income could have been attached to her and, therefore, contends that only a fixed amount ought to have been awarded as compensation on account of her death.

In support of his plea, he seeks to place reliance on the decision of the Apex Court in Lata Wadhwa & Ors. v. State of Bihar & Ors.[(2001) 8 SCC 197].
5.

entities.text: Lata Wadhwa & Ors. v. State of Bihar & Ors.[(2001) 8 SCC 197]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: His final submission is that the learned Tribunal has also erred in awarding interest at the exorbitant rate of 9% per annum.
He, therefore, prays that the interest be reduced to 6% per annum.

He, however, submits that since this Court has already reserved orders in respect of the rate of interest qua the impugned award by way of MAC APP.526/2018 for orders, hearing on this aspect may be deferred for the present.
6.
On the other hand, Mr.Narayan, learned counsel for the respondent by placing reliance on the decision of the Apex Court in Kirti & Anr. v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.

entities.text: Kirti & Anr. v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
[Civil Appeal Nos.19-20/2021] submits that it is no longer res-integra that even in respect of a house-wife,
notional income on the basis of minimum wages, as applicable towards skilled workman, must be taken into account.

While conceding that the impugned award does not make any deduction towards personal expenses of the deceased Smt.Seema Devi, he submits that the award does not grant any amount towards future prospects of the deceased and therefore prays an addition be made under this head.

7. He further submits that the bald plea of the appellant that there were four pillion riders ought to be rejected as it is an admitted position that the appellant neither led any evidence, in this regard before the Tribunal nor cross-examined the witnesses on this aspect.

Furthermore, the learned Tribunal had, after examining the mechanical inspection reports both of the truck as also of the motorcycle, come to a categoric conclusion that the accident took place only on account of the rash and negligent driving of the offending truck.

8. He, however, joins Mr. Gaur in praying that hearing be deferred on the aspect of rate of interest to await the judgement in MAC APP.526/2018.
9.
